title: China's Domestic RF Power Supplies Enter Volume-Production Phase
body: China's domestically produced RF power supplies are moving from single-point technology breakthroughs into volume deployment at fabs, entering what the industry calls a scale-up phase for localization of this core semiconductor-equipment component.

The numbers frame the opportunity and the gap: mainland China's semiconductor RF power market was about RMB 6.56 billion in 2024 with domestic vendors holding less than 12%, while globally MKS and Advanced Energy together control roughly 45%-50% of the market — and over 70% inside China.

Hengyunchang (恒运昌) ranked first among domestic vendors in 2024: its Bestda series stably supports 28nm production lines, its Aspen series is in tool qualification for 7-14nm processes, and its products have been adopted by NAURA, AMEC and Tuojing, with qualification completed at SMIC. Injet Electric's (英杰电气) RHH and RPJ series have entered AMEC's and Tuojing's supply chains and are running at a leading memory fab.

Growth is coming from two tracks: matching newly shipped tools and in-situ replacement on existing lines, with SMIC piloting maintenance-swap programs. Qualification cycles have compressed from over six months to a few months, and domestic vendors compete on 24-48-hour on-site service and fast customization.

title: Huawei's Kirin 9050 Pro Brings 'Logic Folding' to Mass Production
body: Huawei held its first offline Kirin-focused media technology briefing in six years on October 13 at its Shanghai Lianqiu Lake campus, where Xu Songyu, head of Huawei's semiconductor wireless terminal chip product management, detailed the Kirin 9050 Pro — the first mass-produced chip built on Huawei's "logic folding" technology, a program the company started exploring four years ago. The chip also made its first offline public appearance at Huawei's terminal innovation tech event on October 12.

Logic folding is not simple die stacking, Huawei says: the chip is designed from the start with a 3D perspective, distributing logic circuits across multiple co-designed DIEs treated as a single chip, which shortens signal routing, raises transistor density, and improves performance and power efficiency.

The Kirin 9050 series packs over 50 million hybrid bonds and more than 5 million effective signal interconnects, lifting transistor density by 53.5%. For the 9050 Pro specifically, Huawei claims a 12.7% higher CPU clock, 41% better big-core CPU efficiency, 40% higher GPU performance, 45% better GPU efficiency, 140% more NPU compute, and 66% better NPU efficiency.

Hybrid bonding is the key enabler: with a 720nm top-metal pitch, the bond pitch must stay under 2µm (pitch ratio below 3); Huawei says it has reached 1.5µm and targets 1µm in 2027, with tighter pitches unlocking more high-speed channels and deeper folding.

Since Kirin's return to the consumer market in 2023, Huawei devices carrying Kirin chips have shipped over 100 million units, the company said. Xu framed the milestone as validation of "time scaling" as a sustainable path forward: "Even though we have temporarily lost geometry-scaling capability, we can still embark on a new 10-year journey."

title: China's Chip Metrology Market Tops RMB 48 Billion as Local Players Chase Sub-15% Share
body: Mainland China's semiconductor metrology and inspection equipment market has surpassed RMB 48 billion and is growing at a compound rate above 17.5%, yet domestic vendors hold less than 15% — and under 5% in the ultra-high-end segment — leaving what the industry calls one of the deepest localization gaps in the chip supply chain.

Global concentration remains extreme: in 2025 KLA held about 53% of the inspection-systems market, followed by Applied Materials (~15%), ASML (~11%), Hitachi High-Tech (~7.8%) and Tokyo Electron (~5%), with the top five taking 91.8% combined; KLA alone holds close to 60% of the China market. Electron-beam inspection is a roughly US$3.3 billion global market, while advanced-packaging inspection and metrology is about US$925 million.

Suzhou-based startup Precise (普雷赛斯) just closed a Series A round on the order of RMB 100 million backed by investors including E-Town Capital, betting on fully in-house development — its core modules exceed 95% self-developed, spanning optical sensing to AI agents — and focusing on advanced-node and advanced-packaging inspection for TSV, RDL, Bump and HBM processes.

title: Chinese SiC Makers Push Toward 12- and 14-Inch Wafers
body: Four Chinese players have disclosed parallel breakthroughs on oversized silicon carbide, pushing from today's 8-inch ramp straight toward 12- and 14-inch formats: a 12-inch wafer yields about 4.4 times as many chips as a 6-inch one, making size the industry's next cost lever.

Hantian Tiancheng (瀚天天成) reported 12-inch (300mm) n-type 4H-SiC epitaxy with thickness non-uniformity improved from 7.68% to 1.72% and doping non-uniformity from 14.62% to 2.15%, reaching 8-inch-equivalent quality and securing small-batch orders. Shanxi Tiancheng (山西天成) demonstrated a 14-inch SiC single crystal with 30mm effective thickness, 90% localized equipment parts, 60 homegrown growth furnaces in phase one, and a phase-two target of 2028 with about RMB 800 million in annual output.

Lijing Xinke (立晶芯科) has developed an AI-assisted 12-inch crystal-growth system — after its first 8-inch PVT ingot in January 2025 and first liquid-phase ingot in June — and expects a high-quality 12-inch single crystal within two months, with pilot samples next year and mass production the year after. A Zhejiang University team separately produced a ~360mm (about 14-inch) polycrystalline SiC ingot by PVT, reporting room-temperature thermal conductivity of about 323.8 W/(m·K).

title: Lithography Startup Milai Xincheng Raises RMB 361 Million
body: Shanghai-based Milai Xincheng Semiconductor (米莱芯程), a projection-exposure (lithography) equipment maker founded in Pudong in March 2025, is raising RMB 361 million in new capital at a RMB 1.5 billion pre-money valuation, with listed investor United Chemical (联合化学) contributing RMB 60 million.

After the round, United Chemical's stake will be diluted from 37.28% to 33.27%. It is the company's third backing from United Chemical, following RMB 120 million in July 2025 (RMB 500 million valuation) and RMB 200 million in November 2025 (RMB 700 million valuation).

Founder and CTO Gao An previously worked at ASML on DUV and EUV projection lithography. The company posted 2025 revenue of RMB 40.48 million with a net loss of RMB 71.84 million, and first-half 2026 revenue of RMB 8.01 million with a RMB 61.59 million loss.

title: Auto Industry Faces Cost 'High Wall' as Memory Prices Spike Post-Holiday
body: China's auto supply chain is facing across-the-board cost hikes after the Golden Week holiday: more than 60 tire makers issued over 70 price-increase letters since September (2%-5%), carbon black prices rose about 45% within a single month, and rubber futures hit a nine-year high.

Memory chips are automakers' biggest pain point: TrendForce reports global conventional DRAM contract prices rose 90%-95% quarter-on-quarter in Q1 2026, while automotive-grade storage purchase prices jumped about 180% between March and June as AI demand crowds out automotive memory capacity.

UBS estimates memory inflation alone adds RMB 3,000-7,000 to the cost of a high-end ADAS vehicle; NIO said its per-vehicle cost rose roughly RMB 14,000 in Q2 versus end-2025, with memory accounting for about RMB 10,000 of that.

Automakers are fighting back with long-term agreements (GM and Ford both signed LTAs with Micron in July), multi-source battery strategies, and material substitution such as aluminum-for-copper; industry profit still fell 16% year-on-year in January-August with a sales margin of just 3.6%.
The article notes China's automotive chip localization rate topped roughly 35% in the first half of 2026, but high-end compute SoCs and high-safety MCUs remain under 5% localized.

title: Domestic Brands Take Over 60% of China's Servo Market as Industrial 'Chip' Momentum Builds
body: China's 2025 general servo market reached RMB 22.96 billion, with domestic brands topping 60% share for the first time (versus under 50% five years ago), while Japanese brands fell from over 50% before 2020 to about 26%, according to GeWu Zhisheng's market white paper.
Low-voltage inverters tell a similar story: the 2025 market was about RMB 29.27 billion, with local brands climbing to 46% and breaking the long-standing ABB/Siemens dominance.

Invosun (汇川技术) holds roughly 22% servo share as the domestic No.1, ahead of Panasonic and Yaskawa, while StarPower Semiconductor earned Invosun's 'strategic supplier' honor in January 2026 with custom-developed IGBT and SiC modules.

Local power-device makers are evolving from build-to-spec suppliers into co-definition partners: Silan Micro is advancing an 'MCU + power module + driver IC' integrated portfolio, and MacroMicro is building a 'chip + module' platform across new energy, EVs, and data centers.

Caveats remain: high-end IGBT modules, precision SiC devices, and high-end IPM modules still lag by a generation and depend heavily on imports, while wide-bandgap cost barriers are slowing large-scale penetration.

title: CW Lasers Emerge as the Tightest Link in the CPO Supply Chain
body: As CPO architecture moves the light source out of the module, a single ultra-high-power CW laser must deliver 400mW of output fiber power and hold it at 55°C or higher; per Coherent's ECOC 2026 architecture, one external light source (ELS) packs up to 8 UHP CW lasers, each split across roughly four links.

Only Lumentum and Coherent publicly supply 400mW-class devices: Nvidia invested $2 billion in each in March 2026 with multi-year purchase commitments, and Coherent said indium phosphide remains its main internal constraint even as June-quarter InP laser output rose about 80% year-on-year.

Domestic vendors are 'delivered at the low end, qualifying at the high end': Yuanjie ships 70mW and 100mW CW lasers in volume (first-half revenue of RMB 925 million, up 351.4% year-on-year, with net profit up 1,212.2%), while its 120mW/300mW/400mW chips are still in qualification; Shijia Photonics ships non-cooled 100mW CW DFB in volume and room-temperature 400mW CW DFB in small volume.

Sanan Optoelectronics plans 400mW sampling for 3.2T optical switches in Q4 2026 with volume shipments in Q1 2027; Accelink and Hisense's Nazhen have high-power models in customer qualification, and Accelink is investing about RMB 6.75 billion toward 800G/1.6T/3.2T capacity.
The article concludes that the real race is not lighting up 400mW in the lab, but ramping yield and capacity at the same time once qualification clears.

title: Domestic Five-Phase Stepper Motors Challenge Long-Standing Japanese Dominance
body: China's 2025 stepper market exceeded RMB 3.2 billion, with industrial steppers at about RMB 2 billion (up 5% year-on-year), per MIR; five-phase steppers — prized for smaller step angles and smoother motion — were long dominated by Japan's Oriental Motor PK/PKP series.

Founded in 2015, Ruite Technology launched a 20mm-flange five-phase motor in 2026 with a 0.72° step angle, filling the hard-to-develop small-frame gap and now covering 20/28/42/60mm — one of the most complete domestic lineups.
Side-by-side repeat-positioning tests of Ruite's 28CM005-D V3.0 against a leading Japanese product on the same drive and platform showed comparable precision.

Ruite's high-performance five-phase solutions are already in volume use on 400G, 800G, and 1.6T optical-module coupling machines, achieving ±0.05μm repeat positioning on XYZ axes in 12-axis FA coupling systems.
The article frames this as domestic steppers moving from single-model replacement toward full product-line coverage of the precision segment.

title: Skyworks Closes $22 Billion Qorvo Merger, Creating RF Powerhouse
body: Skyworks Solutions has completed its previously announced combination with Qorvo, a cash-and-stock transaction valued at approximately $22 billion when it was first announced in October 2025; the deal closed on October 5, 2026 after clearing all regulatory approvals.

Under the terms, Qorvo shareholders received $32.50 in cash plus 0.960 of a Skyworks share for each Qorvo share, leaving legacy Skyworks holders with roughly 63% of the combined company and former Qorvo holders with about 37% on a fully diluted basis.

The combined business keeps the Skyworks name and the SWKS ticker on Nasdaq, and brings together around 8,000 engineers and more than 12,000 issued and pending patents, adding RF GaN, low-voltage power and wired broadband to the portfolio.
Skyworks said the merger more than doubles its addressable market, extending beyond smartphones into defense and aerospace, data center and networking, automotive, edge IoT and AI infrastructure.

The company expects at least $500 million in annualized cost synergies within 24 to 36 months and said the transaction is immediately accretive to non-GAAP earnings per share; part of the cash consideration was financed with $2 billion in senior notes issued in August 2026.

title: Mature-Node Foundry Prices Climb Again in 2026 as 8-Inch Capacity Shrinks
body: Price-hike signals in 2026 have spread from advanced compute and memory into 8-inch foundry services, select 12-inch mature processes, and power devices, with eefocus describing the repricing as structural rather than a repeat of the 2021 shortage.

The timeline: SMIC notified customers late last year of an ~10% increase on 8-inch BCD platforms; TrendForce's January survey found some fabs planning 5%-20% increases; and Chinese power-device vendors including CR Micro, Yangjie, Silan, NCE and MacroMicro announced February adjustments covering MOSFETs, IGBTs and related products.

Through mid-year, Infineon moved customers to new prices effective April 1, STMicroelectronics raised prices in March and again from June 28, and TrendForce's end-June survey showed ~5%-15% average increases on 8-inch foundry across the first half, with 5%-10% increases emerging on tight 12-inch mature nodes in Q2-Q3.

On the capacity side, TrendForce projects TSMC and Samsung will shrink 8-inch capacity faster than additions from SMIC and Vanguard can offset, leaving global 8-inch capacity down ~2.4% year-on-year in 2026.

A key driver is AI: AI server power chains are lifting demand for power management, gate drivers, MOSFETs, DrMOS and smart power stages — demand that runs on mature platforms rather than leading-edge logic.

title: Empyrean's Liu Weiping: Domestic EDA Crosses 'Usable' Threshold, Agentic AI May Reshape the Industry
body: Speaking at CIIF 2026's dedicated IC exhibition in Shanghai on October 12, Empyrean Technology chairman Liu Weiping said commercially deployable domestic EDA tools now cover about 85% of design needs, with nearly 10% at world-leading levels; process-node ecosystem coverage stands near 50% and is targeted at 80% this year.
Empyrean serves nearly 800 customers globally, including seven or eight of the world's top ten chip designers, with more than 6,000 chips designed using its tools.

Liu set three next-phase tasks for China's EDA: supporting indigenous advanced processes, adapting to new 'folded' circuit design methodologies that foreign tools will not support, and rebuilding tool efficiency with AI — where agentic EDA, he said, could change the shape of the entire industry.

title: Hua Hong's Bai Peng: US$1 Trillion Chip Market Arrives a Year Early; Mature Specialty Nodes 'Must Not Be Ignored'
body: At CIIF 2026 in Shanghai, Hua Hong Semiconductor chairman and president Bai Peng said the global IC market will cross US$1 trillion in 2026 — a year earlier than the previously forecast 2027 — driven by AI compute infrastructure and a memory rebound.

The mature-process (22nm and above) foundry market is expected to exceed US$60 billion in 2026, about 27% of global foundry, he said, with mature nodes growing around 6.8% annually — still a stable-growth market, not a shrinking one.

China's foundry capacity now accounts for one-third of the global total, expanding at over 10% CAGR versus 4-5% worldwide; Hua Hong aims to lift its specialty-process ASP ratio from 66% in 2024 to 76% by 2030, targeting 30%, 50%, 20%, 40% and 35% global foundry shares in eFlash, SPI NOR, BCD, CIS and discrete devices respectively by 2030.

title: Xianyi Micro Closes Series A to Scale Magnetic-Isolation Chips, Sets Up East China HQ in Wuxi
body: Shenzhen-based Xianyi Microelectronics, which says it is China's first commercial magnetic-isolation chip company, has closed a Series A round worth tens of millions of yuan led by Xizhou International, and established its East China headquarters in Binhu, Wuxi.

The company says it built China's first commercial magnetic-isolation process line and now offers nearly 300 magnetic-isolation products across signal, interface, driver and power lines, with automotive products AEC-Q100 qualified and in volume supply for industrial and energy-storage applications.

The Wuxi base will serve as its East China R&D and support center, tapping the Yangtze River Delta customer cluster as demand grows in AI compute power infrastructure, solid-state transformers and embodied intelligence — areas where high-voltage isolation requirements are intensifying.

title: Four SiC Projects in China Accelerate Toward Production
body: Four silicon carbide projects across China reported fresh progress this week, signaling continued capacity expansion in the third-generation semiconductor race.

Lips' Yangzhou SiC project, a provincial major project with total investment of 1 billion yuan (180 million yuan in phase one), will deliver its first phase — two automotive-grade SiC module packaging and testing lines with annual capacity of 1.5 million units — by year-end 2026; full build-out targets 3 million units per year.

Galaxy Microelectronics topped out the main structure of its Changzhou base on October 8 and expects trial production in Q2 next year; at full capacity it will produce 50 million IGBT and SiC power modules annually.

Xinjia Electronics said its fully automated automotive-grade SiC module line is already running at full load with 600,000 units of annual capacity, with products qualified into supply chains of leading domestic automakers; two more lines planned for next year would lift capacity to 1.5 million automotive-grade and 4 million industrial-grade units per year by late 2027 or early 2028.
Zhongyi Chuangxin reported its optical-grade SiC powder project — supplying semi-insulating SiC powder for AR glasses lenses — is 80% complete since construction began in June.

title: Global AI Compute Market Nears US$1.2 Trillion in 2026, Industry Data Shows
body: Industry research reports cited in the coverage put global computing capacity at 4,495 EFlops as of June 2025, up 117% year on year, with intelligent computing accounting for 85% of the total — marking a structural shift from general to intelligent computing.

The global AI compute market is approaching US$1.2 trillion in 2026; the AI semiconductor market is estimated at about US$485 billion this year, on track for roughly US$753 billion by 2030, while global semiconductor spending hit US$793 billion in 2025, up 21%.

Capital is flooding in: global data center capex rose 57% in 2025 and is expected to exceed US$1 trillion in 2026, driven by more than 10 million high-end accelerators, with AI infrastructure spending already surpassing US$1.3 trillion.

China's computing capacity reached 962 EFlops — about 21% of the global total, up 73% year on year — and domestic AI accelerator shipments keep climbing: Nvidia holds about 55% of China's AI card market (2.2 million units), domestic vendors a combined 41% (1.65 million), and AMD and others about 4% of a roughly 4-million-unit total.

title: TSMC Taps GlobalFoundries in US$2 Billion Silicon Interposer Deal for CoWoS
body: GlobalFoundries announced on October 8 a multi-year manufacturing agreement with TSMC: GF will expand silicon interposer capacity at its Malta, New York fab to supply TSMC's CoWoS advanced-packaging ecosystem, in a deal worth an estimated US$2 billion over an initial five-year term, with volume ramp expected in the first half of 2028.
The deal makes GF the first US-based supplier of silicon interposers for advanced packaging, adding a clear supply-chain regionalization dimension to what is otherwise a pure capacity play.

Counterpoint Research estimates TSMC's CoWoS supply-demand gap at about 20% in 2026, narrowing to roughly 10% in 2027 as internal capacity expands toward 185,000 wafers per month; TrendForce expects TSMC's 2026 average monthly CoWoS capacity at 120,000–140,000 wafers — a record — with 2027 capacity up more than 60%.

Yole Group data cited in the coverage puts the global advanced-packaging market at about US$44.3 billion in 2022, growing to roughly US$78.6 billion by 2028 at a compound annual rate of around 10%, with AI demand as the core driver.

The mystery "Party A" in Synaptics' October 8 proxy filing is Cirrus Logic, which made an unsolicited rival bid in September after onsemi's approach, Bloomberg reported citing people familiar with the matter.
onsemi revised its proposal on October 1 to an all-cash transaction worth about US$5.7 billion (US$123 per share), replacing its original all-stock offer valued at roughly US$7 billion.
title: Cirrus Logic Named as Rival Bidder for Synaptics as onsemi Switches to All-Cash Offer

body: Nomura expects China's wafer-fab equipment market to grow at a compound rate of about 19% from FY2025 to FY2030, lifting China's chip self-sufficiency from roughly 34% in FY2025 to about 47% in FY2030.
Upstream wafer suppliers are moving first: Shin-Etsu Chemical, SUMCO and GlobalWafers have all announced two rounds of price increases for 2026.
title: Nomura: China's Semiconductor Equipment Market Could Top US$100 Billion in FY2027

body: AMD's space-grade Versal AI Core XQRVC1902 is now sampling with early customers and is aimed at MIL-PRF-38535 Class Y, the highest reliability certification for space electronics.
The lidless organic package is designed for missions lasting up to 15 years and is fully pin-compatible with the existing VC1902 device family.
title: AMD Ships Space-Grade Versal XQRVC1902 Targeting 15-Year Missions

body: Microchip announced on October 9 that it has acquired VORAGO Technologies, an Austin-based private company whose radiation-hardened chips operate in high-radiation environments and at temperatures up to 200°C, serving aerospace, defense and industrial mission-critical applications.
Terms were not disclosed; Microchip said the acquisition will have no material impact on combined financial results. The deal strengthens its aerospace and defense solutions portfolio.
title: Microchip Acquires Radiation-Hardened Chipmaker VORAGO Technologies

body: Infineon's new automotive-grade cluster MCU, the TRAVEO T2G CYT4EN, pairs with external LPDDR4 memory to render 2.5D graphics and 3D content, driving dual Full HD displays without a separate SoC.
The memory subsystem was co-optimized with Micron, the chip supports ASIL-B functional safety, boots in under 150 milliseconds, and is available now.
title: Infineon Launches TRAVEO T2G CYT4EN Automotive Cluster MCU

body: Samsung has told its supply chain it will cut fourth-quarter phone supply by 20–30%, as surging memory prices erase handset margins.

AI data centers have diverted wafer capacity away from mobile DRAM, pushing mobile memory contract prices up 175% over the past year. Samsung's full-year phone output is now expected at around 200 million units, down from 270 million.
title: Samsung Cuts Q4 Phone Supply by up to 30% as Memory Prices Bite

body: The reference design, announced October 5, collapses rack power conversion from two stages to one — converting 800V DC directly to 6V DC and skipping the intermediate 50V bus.

It targets 96% full-load efficiency and 2,100 W/in³ power density, pairing Microchip's dsPIC33AK digital controller with 16 Navitas NV6034 GaN FETs. Reference boards, software and design documentation open to developers at the OCP Global Summit in San Jose, October 12–15.
title: Navitas and Microchip Unveil 800V Reference Design for AI Data Centers

body: Samsung has pre-committed roughly 75–80% of next year's memory capacity to long-term agreements, with Nvidia, Google and Microsoft seeking supply locks of five years or more.
The memory business is shifting from quarterly pricing to a long-term-contract model, leaving shrinking spot availability for distributors and the open market.
title: Samsung Locks Up 75–80% of 2027 Memory Output in Long-Term Deals

body: NXP's Ara240, a discrete neural-network processor for the edge delivering up to 40 eTOPS, enables local inference of LLMs and vision-language models without cloud dependency.
Mouser began stocking the part on October 5. The chip pairs with 16 GB of LPDDR4, connects via PCIe Gen4 and USB 3.2, and includes secure boot with a hardware root of trust.
title: NXP Ara240 Edge AI Processor Hits Mouser Shelves

body: AMD CEO Lisa Su said in Taipei on October 6 that demand has outstripped supply and the company plans to substantially increase chip supply in 2027.
The Asia trip is capacity-focused: meetings with Foxconn and TSMC in Taiwan, plus planned talks with Samsung and SK Hynix in Korea on memory supply.
title: AMD Plans Substantial Supply Increase in 2027, CEO Says

body: ST launched two 6-axis IMUs with dual accelerometers in a single package: the consumer-grade LSM6DSK320X and the industrial-grade ISM6HGK256X.

A symmetric mirrored gyroscope structure cancels vibration and shock, while the dual accelerometers capture micro-motion and high-g events simultaneously without range switching. Ranges span ±16g to ±320g, the industrial part is rated from −40°C to +105°C, and adapter boards ship from November 2026.
title: ST Adds Dual-Accelerometer 6-Axis IMUs

body: Taiwan prosecutors indicted ten people for buying controlled chips from Analog Devices and Texas Instruments under the guise of a Taiwanese research institute since 2017, relabeling chips made in overseas factories as "Made in Taiwan" and reselling them to China via Hong Kong.
Prosecutors are seeking a 10-year sentence for the ringleader; illicit profits totaled NT$300 million (about US$9.4 million).
title: Taiwan Indicts 10 for Relabeling US-Controlled Chips for Resale to China

body: Samsung's preliminary third-quarter results set a record at 107.4 trillion won, driven almost entirely by the memory business, with memory margins reportedly exceeding Nvidia's.
HBM is consuming a disproportionate share of wafer capacity, and brokerages expect the rally in conventional memory to extend into next year.
title: Samsung's Memory Margins Top Nvidia's as Q3 Profit Hits Record

body: Infineon has completed its acquisition of Bangalore-based C2i Semiconductor, buying its digital power-control capabilities for AI data center power.
C2i's software-defined multiphase controllers and smart power stages will be integrated with Infineon's silicon, SiC and GaN power semiconductor portfolios.
title: Infineon Completes Acquisition of C2i Semiconductor

body: Microchip's MTCH3380P and MTCH3240P are its first turnkey touch controllers for buttons, sliders and wheels in screenless HMI, with 12 on-chip ADCs sampling touch signals in parallel so responsiveness holds as sensor counts grow.
The MTCH3380P is priced at US$1.06 and the MTCH3240P at US$0.80 in 10,000-unit quantities.
title: Microchip Debuts First Parallel-Sensing Touch Controllers

body: ASML issued a rare blanket price increase to Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix: all EUV and DUV lithography parts for the Korean market rise 10% for deliveries from January 2027.
If the two Korean fabs accept, the move sets a precedent for Applied Materials, Tokyo Electron and other equipment vendors to follow with their own increases.
title: ASML Raises All Lithography Parts Prices 10% for Korean Market

body: Infineon released a three-phase PSU reference design for AI server racks built entirely from its own parts — CoolSiC and CoolMOS, EiceDRIVER, XENSIV sensors and PSoC — with peak efficiency above 98%.
The design debuts at the OCP Global Summit in San Jose starting October 12.
title: Infineon Unveils 27 kW 3-Phase PSU for AI Server Racks
Eswei Computing Lists in Hong Kong as "First RISC-V Stock," Valued at HK$35.4 Billion
body: Beijing Eswei Computing (01256.HK) debuted on the HKEX main board on October 9 at HK$1.55 per share, closing day one at HK$1.605 for a market capitalization of HK$35.4 billion. Founded in 2019 by BOE founder Wang Dongsheng, the company is China's largest domestic supplier of human-machine-interface chips and ranks third among Chinese vendors in RISC-V controller chips.

Revenue grew from RMB 1.75 billion in 2023 to RMB 2.43 billion in 2025, though cumulative net losses over the period reached RMB 4.9 billion on R&D spending that has long exceeded half of revenue. The bright spot is the computing-chip business: its revenue share jumped from 13.2% in 2025 to 45.1% in Q1 2026, driven by a RISC-V AI SoC program for large-model inference already adopted by a leading consumer storage maker.
The roughly HK$2.4 billion raised will fund chip R&D, RISC-V ecosystem building and potential strategic acquisitions.

title: Wolfspeed Secures US$1.5 Billion Conditional Loan from US Department of War for GaN-on-SiC
body: Wolfspeed announced on October 7 that it has received a conditional commitment letter from the US Department of War's Office of Strategic Capital for up to US$1.5 billion in 30-year financing to build a domestic wide-bandgap semiconductor supply chain. The funding will upgrade its GaN epitaxy capabilities for next-generation communications infrastructure and electronic-warfare systems, and develop radiation-hardened technology for SiC and future GaN products.
As part of the arrangement, Wolfspeed expects to issue warrants to the Department of War for up to 7.5% of its fully diluted equity, disbursed pro rata with funding tranches.

The move sharpens a strategic pivot: after selling its GaN-on-SiC RF business to MACOM for US$125 million in 2023, Wolfspeed has shifted from an RF-device IDM model to a materials supplier focused on semi-insulating SiC substrates and GaN epitaxy.

title: Bluetooth Chip Shipments to Hit 10.3 Billion by 2032 as Growth Shifts to Data Bluetooth
body: Global Bluetooth chip shipments will grow from 8.3 billion units in 2025 to 10.3 billion in 2032, a 3.2% CAGR, according to Techno Systems Research's 2026 Wireless Connectivity Market Analysis. The bigger story is the mix shift: audio Bluetooth SoCs still hold 61% share in 2025, but data Bluetooth is catching up fast, with the two segments expected to reach roughly 50:50 by 2031–2032 as IoT applications expand.

In BLE single-mode SoCs, Nordic Semiconductor leads with 21% of shipments and 36% of revenue. Four Chinese vendors including Telink and PHYPlus hold a combined 29% of shipments but only 9% of revenue — a low-price strategy concentrated at the mid-to-low end.
Edge AI is becoming the key differentiator for BLE SoCs, moving from TinyML toward DSP/NPU-integrated parts for sensor fusion and on-device inference, with Nordic and Silicon Labs in the lead.

title: Beijing Shimu Microelectronics Closes Series B+ Round Led by Industrial Investors
body: Beijing Shimu Microelectronics (士模微电子), a high-performance signal-chain chipmaker, has closed a Series B+ financing round of undisclosed size, with the checks written by downstream customers — test-equipment maker Shenzhen Jingzhida and CRRC Times High-Tech Investment. Founded in 2021 by Tsinghua professor and IEEE Fellow Nan Sun, the company targets data converters, the hardest analog segment to localize.

Its high-speed, high-precision ADC CM3452 consumes about 960 mW, roughly one-third of international competitors, and is reportedly the first such chip taped out and mass-produced at a domestic foundry.

The deal highlights a structural gap: China consumes about one-third of the world's analog chips, yet overall self-sufficiency is only 16–18%, falling to 10–15% in industrial grades and about 5% in automotive, where high-end ADCs remain dominated by TI and ADI.

title: Domestic Brands Take Over 60% of China's Servo Market as Industrial Chip Localization Deepens
body: China's general servo market rebounded to RMB 23 billion in 2025, with domestic brands capturing over 60% share for the first time — up from under 50% five years ago — while Japanese brands fell from over 50% to about 26%, according to a 2026 industry white paper. In low-voltage inverters, a RMB 29.3 billion market, domestic brands reached 46%, breaking long-standing foreign monopolies.

Local power-device makers are graduating from pure suppliers to strategic partners co-defining products with machine builders: StarPower develops custom IGBT/SiC modules with Inovance, while Silan fields an integrated "MCU + power module + gate-driver IC" portfolio.

Gaps remain at the high end — domestic high-end IGBT/SiC modules still lag in long-term reliability and batch consistency, and SiC cost barriers are slowing adoption in mid-to-low-end equipment, where price wars are squeezing R&D budgets.

title: onsemi's Second 2026 Price Hike Takes Effect — Power Semis in a Full Upcycle
body: onsemi's second price increase of 2026 takes effect today (October 10), covering a broad range of product lines. The company cites persistently rising costs across raw materials, manufacturing, energy and infrastructure — alongside growing demand from power, industrial and datacenter markets. It follows an earlier round of increases in the first half of the year.

This is not an isolated move. 2026 has turned into a broad-based power-semiconductor repricing: Texas Instruments, Infineon and STMicroelectronics have all implemented increases, Renesas has announced its second hike (effective January 2027), and Taiwan suppliers are reportedly planning 10–15% increases on spot products from October.

Behind the cost pass-through sits a genuine demand shift: as AI rack power climbs toward the megawatt range, power architectures are migrating from 48V to 800V HVDC — lifting per-rack content for SiC, GaN and high-efficiency MOSFETs.
